classes.name: Stortingsvalg
classes.finest_note: Each constituency is one contest; valgresultat.no publishes counts by polling circuit from 2009, SSB by municipality from 1906 (NOS volumes) and in Statistikkbanken for recent elections.
classes.note: 169 members (since 2005) in 19 constituencies, the counties of 2019: 150 district seats by modified Sainte-Laguë (first divisor 1.4) among closed lists, and one leveling seat per constituency for parties above 4% nationally. Direct elections since 1906: single-member constituencies with a second ballot until 1918, list PR since 1921. The Storting cannot be dissolved (Grunnloven § 71), so elections fall every fourth September. Before 1906 see storting_indirekte.

classes.name: Kommunestyrevalg
classes.finest_note: Each municipality is one contest; valgresultat.no by polling circuit from 2011, SSB by municipality from 1945 (votes) and 1901 (national totals).
classes.note: Every municipal council (kommunestyre; bystyre in towns) is elected for four years on the same September Monday as the county councils, by open lists with personal votes and modified Sainte-Laguë; where only one list or none is filed, by majority vote. Municipal elections go back to the formannskapslover of 1837; universal suffrage from 1910. Councils elected in 2019 and 2023 served the merged municipalities of 2020 and 2024. Extraordinary elections are held only for new merged municipalities (Færder, 2017).

classes.name: Valg til bydelsutvalg i Oslo
classes.finest_note: Oslo kommune publishes each district council's result by party; counts by polling circuit are not known to be published.
classes.note: Oslo's 15 district councils (bydelsutvalg) are elected directly from party lists on the day of the municipal election, under the regulation on direct elections to submunicipal councils (kommuneloven § 5-8). A trial with four directly elected district councils ran in 1995; all have been directly elected since 2007.

access.evidence: Results of the bystyre and bydelsutvalg elections for 2007 and later, with each district council's settlement (valgoppgjør).

dates.note: A trial with four directly elected district councils in 1995, and direct elections in every district by 2007 (Oslo kommune publishes district council results from 2007); not yet counted from Oslo kommune's result pages.

classes.name: Valg til Longyearbyen lokalstyre
classes.finest_note: One contest per election; results by party only.
classes.note: The local council of Longyearbyen on Svalbard, created by the 2001 amendment of the Svalbard Act and in office from 1 January 2002, is elected by list PR under a regulation of 14 May 2007 (no. 506) in October of the municipal election year. Since 2023 non-Nordic foreign residents need three years of residence in a Norwegian municipality to vote.

classes.name: Forsøk med direkte valg av ordfører
classes.finest_note: One contest per trial municipality, two rounds where no candidate won a majority; results are in the trial municipalities' records and the ministry's evaluations.
classes.note: Under the Local Government Act's trial provision, the ministry let 20 municipalities in 1999 and 36 in 2003 elect the mayor directly on the municipal election day, with a second round. The Storting declined in 2006-2007 to make it permanent, and the trials ended.

dates.note: The Odelsting committee's report gives 37.

classes.name: Lokale folkeavstemninger
classes.finest_note: One contest per vote (a few span a county); SSB counts them by topic and gives electorate and turnout, not the yes and no votes.
classes.note: Consultative votes held by a municipal or county council under kommuneloven § 12-1 on any matter, most often alcohol sales, the written standard of Norwegian for schools, and boundary changes. SSB counts 992 from 1970 to 2025, 204 of them in 2016 on the municipal reform.

access.evidence: Counts of local referendums by topic and year (07552), and electorate and turnout by municipality (07548); no vote counts by option.

dates.note: Most were consultative votes on the municipal mergers of the 2014-2020 reform.

classes.name: Kirkevalg i Den norske kirke
classes.disposition_reason: Parish councils (menighetsråd) and diocesan councils are elected by the members of the Church of Norway under the church's own election rules (trossamfunnsloven § 10, the General Synod's regulations), held on the same days as public elections but run by the church; the electorate is church membership, not a public electorate.

classes.name: Kongen og regjeringen
classes.disposition_reason: The King is hereditary (Grunnloven § 6), and the Prime Minister and government are appointed by the King and depend on the Storting's confidence; there is no popular vote for an executive.

classes.name: Valg av ordfører og fylkesordfører
classes.disposition_reason: Mayors and county mayors are elected by and from the municipal and county councils (kommuneloven § 6-1); only the 1999 and 2003 trials (direkte_ordforer) were popular votes.

classes.name: Amtsting og fylkesting valgt av kommunestyrene (1837-1975)
classes.name_en: County councils chosen by the municipal councils (1837-1975)
classes.disposition_reason: Until 1963 the amtsting/fylkesting was made up of the mayors of the rural municipalities, and from 1964 to 1975 its members were chosen by the municipal councils; there was no popular vote.

classes.name: Lagtinget og Odelstinget (1814-2009)
classes.disposition_reason: The Storting chose a quarter of its own members as the Lagting, the rest forming the Odelsting; the divisions were abolished from the 2009 Storting. Not a popular vote.

classes.name: Dommere og meddommere
classes.disposition_reason: Professional judges are appointed by the King in Council on the Judicial Appointments Board's recommendation; lay judges and conciliation board members are chosen by the municipal and county councils (domstolloven §§ 64-66, 27). No popular vote.

classes.name: Nominasjon av kandidater
classes.disposition_reason: Parties nominate their lists at their own nomination meetings (valgloven ch. 6 sets only the filing rules); the state runs no primaries and publishes no nomination results.
